title: Spain – Refrigerating equipment – Helium Refrigeration System (HRS) for Isotope Separation System (ISS) of ITER Fuel Cycle
description: The scope of this procurement procedure is the design, manufacturing, assembly, factory acceptance testing, transport and delivery of the Helium Refrigeration System (HRS) for the Isotope Separation System (ISS) within the Tritium Plant at ITER, based on Reversed Turbo-Brayton technology. The HRS will supply a cooling net power of approximately 1500 W at 18.5 K for the ISS of the ITER Tritium Plant. Optional scope: Option 1: factory performance testing; Option 2: technical assistance for on-site installation and final connection activities; Option 3: technical assistance for commissioning and site acceptance testing. Before the final call for tender, F4E may decide to remove certain options from the scope.

title: Ireland – Security services – T.083.2026 Request for Tenders to establish a Single-Supplier Framework for the provision of Temporary CCTV and related Services for Special Events as a Managed Service, for An Garda Síochána
description: In summary, the services requested comprise of the provision of temporary CCTV and related Services for outdoor Special Events and VIP Visits as a Managed Service. The Contracting Authority will require the successful Tenderer to have the ability to provide services they are tendering for within short notice i.e. 48 hours. The Contracting Authority will establish a single-supplier framework for the provision of the following services individually or in combination to support policing operations during special events (including VIP visits): • The provision of CCTV Services (including the provision, installation and maintenance of cameras, video links, and a video evidence management solution); • The provision of a communications vehicle (or vehicles) with equipment necessary to provide control room functionality and to support incident management); • The provision of large (outdoor) video displays; and, • The provision of a public announcement (“PA”) system (or systems). The successful Tenderer will be responsible for sourcing and providing the equipment listed above along with the provision of ancillary services and equipment necessary to provide the equipment above as a managed service.

title: Q702--Gainesville OPC IOTA
description: Department of Veterans Affairs Veterans Health Administration Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) August 13, 2026 PRESOLICITATION NOTICE Initial Outfitting, Transition, and Activation Services in support of the Gainesville, FL OPC 100% SDVOSB SET ASIDE This is a Pre-Solicitation Notice that the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) intends to solicit quotes to provide non-personal Initial Outfitting, Transition, and Activation (IOT&A) services for Gainesville, FL Outpatient Clinic (OPC). This requirement supports VHA's mission by providing contractor support services to help bring the hospital into full planned operations that will provide health care services to Veterans. This will be a firm-fixed-price contract with an estimated Period of Performance of 46-months. The North Florida/South Georgia Healthcare System has been approved for a major lease to create an expanded service opportunity for Veteran health care at Gainesville OPC Consolidation. This project proposes to lease a new outpatient clinic in Gainesville, FL. This project is approximately 188,418 net usable square foot (NUSF) in the vicinity of Gainesville, FL, including 1300 parking spaces. The clinic will expand on care currently provided at the existing contracted lease spaces and allow an expansion to the current footprint as well as added new for a decompression of the Malcom Randall VA Medical Center (VAMC) in Gainesville, FL. The lease would allow VA to consolidate outpatient services at one location for mental health, home based primary care, specialty care and ancillary diagnostics identified in the Strategic Capital Investment Planning (SCIP) process. The scope includes project support for planning, activating, outfitting, and transitioning the staff and Veterans/patients associated with the project The scope includes project support for planning, activating, outfitting, and transitioning the staff and Veterans/patients associated with the project. The scope of services includes Comprehensive Project Management, Comprehensive Interior Design, FF&E, and Space Planning Support; CONOPS and Transitioning Planning; Acquisition Support Services to include package development, Activation, Delivery, Relocation and Installation, Training, and Turnover and Post Occupancy Support for the identified project. This requirement will be set-aside 100% for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs) using FAR Part 12 and 37. To be eligible for an SDVOSB set aside under VA s Veterans First Contracting Program, SDVOSBs must: be verified by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) as SDVOSB (see https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ for details) and meet the small business size standard for NAICS 541614. The solicitation is anticipated to be posted on Contract Opportunities for download on or about 10 September 2026. Potential offerors are advised that there may be truncated response time on the solicitation that will follow this Pre-Solicitation notice. Anticipated closing date of the solicitation will be 9 October 2026. Solicitation initial posting date and the closing date are subject to change as necessary. Any questions for this Pre-solicitation notice should be sent via e-mail to both Katherine.Johnson@va.gov and Kathleen.Klotzbach@va.gov. No telephone requests/questions will be accepted. This Pre-Solicitation notice does not constitute a request for proposals. P.O.C: Katherine.Johnson@va.gov, Contract Specialist and Kathleen.Klotzbach@va.gov, Contracting Officer

title: Passenger air terminal services at Naval Air Station Jacksonville, FL
description: Amendment 0002 posted 22 September 2026, is posted with updated Attachment 2 PWS rev 2, updated Conformed Solicitation N6883626QS049 0002, and provide answers to questions received as Attachment QandA. Please submit pricing on the Conformed Solicitation N6883626QS049 0002. Acknowledge by signing the amendment and return with any quote documentation. Amendment 0001 posted 11 September 2026, is posted with updated Attachment 2 PWS, provide Attachment 4 Wage Determination 2015-4539, and provide answers to questions received. Please acknowledge by signing the amendment and return with any quote documentation. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number N6883626QS049 is issued as a request for quote (RFQ), for Passenger air terminal services at Naval Air Station Jacksonville, FL. The services to be furnished under this contract provide Passenger Terminal Services in support of the Defense Transportation System (DTS) to include, but not limited to, all United States (U.S.) Government owned or operated aircraft; U.S. sponsored foreign Government or civil aircraft, Coalition Forces aircraft, North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO), commercial contract aircraft, and commercial tendered aircraft. Services must facilitate on time aircraft departures and maintain the ability to provide sustained Passenger Terminal Services for a working Maximum on Ground (WMOG) capability of one wide-body aircraft or any combination of narrow-body aircraft which equate to one wide body aircraft. This acquisition is set aside for small business concerns. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. Refer to attached RFQ for more information. Questions from responsible, interested business parties regarding the solicitation must be submitted by email to Peiney Allerton at Peiney.t.allerton.civ@us.navy.mil or harold.m.melton.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 10:00 EDT, 21 SEP 2026. Quotes submitted in response to the solicitation must be submitted by email to Peiney Allerton at Peiney.t.allerton.civ@us.navy.mil or harold.m.melton.civ@us.navy.mil no later than 10:00 EDT, 09 OCT 2026.

description: This is the Stage 1 process for the Establishment of a Multi-Party Framework Agreement for Minor Building Works Residential for Tipperary County Council. This framework has the potential to be established for 4years estimated from early Jan 2027 until end Dec 2030. The scope of the Framework will include any building works which may be required within any of the 5no. Municipal Districts of County Tipperary; 1. Nenagh District 2. Templemore-Thurles District 3. Cahir, Cashel, Tipperary District 4. Clonmel District 5. Carrick-on-Suir District. Works within this Framework may include but are not limited to general repairs, maintenance to the building fabric, roofing works, modifications for disability access, internal external modification and alterations to buildings, electrical works, plumbing, heating and mechanical system works, replacement of windows and internal and external doors, installation modification kitchens, floor coverings, painting and decorating, suspended ceiling works, dry‐lining, jointing and plastering, construction of small extensions, minor demolition works, clearance works in preparation for re‐letting re‐occupation, external site works such as driveways, steps, paths, fences and boundary walls, landscaping, drainage and residential waste and foul water treatment works. title: Netherlands – Street-lighting maintenance services – Versneld verledden gemeente Beuningen
description: De werkzaamheden binnen dit bestek hebben betrekking op de renovatie van de openbare verlichtingsinstallatie (OVL). De werkzaamheden bestaan in hoofdzaak uit: - Het leveren van masten en armaturen - Het vervangen, monteren en aansluiten van verlichtingsobjecten, masten, armaturen - Het coördineren van werkzaamheden aan het gereguleerde netwerk - Rapporteren van de verrichte werkzaamheden - Het aanleveren van revisiegegevens Betreft de vervanging van ca. 2000 verlichtingsarmaturen en ca. 400 verlichtingsobjecten/masten. Voor de uitvoering van de opdracht is een maximaal budget beschikbaar van €1.130.000, exclusief btw. Het beschikbare budget vormt een harde financiële randvoorwaarde voor deze aanbesteding. Indien de laagste geldige inschrijfsom, zoals opgegeven op het inschrijvingsbiljet, hoger is dan €1.130.000, exclusief btw, zal de aanbestedende dienst de opdracht niet gunnen, omdat het beschikbare budget ontoereikend is. description: Combined Synopsis and Solicitation This is a combined synopsis and solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotations are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. Request for Quote (RFQ) number is N6660426Q00466. The Naval Undersea Warfare Center Division, Newport (NUWCDIVNPT) intends to award a purchase order to Workplace Modular Systems LLC on a Sole Source basis for Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) Benches detailed in the table below. Workplace Modular Systems LLC is the only qualified source capable of providing these components to meet all the functional and performance parameters required within the Government�s infrastructure. These components are used to prevent electrostatic discharge from disrupting the electronics during testing. The notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals. Delivery shall be FOB Destination, Newport, RI. Incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through the most current Federal Acquisition Circular (FAC). The following clauses and provisions apply to this solicitation: - FAR 52.209-11, Representation by Corporations Regarding Delinquent Tax Liability or a Felony Conviction under any Federal Law (FEB 2016) - FAR 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors--Commercial Products and Commercial Services - FAR 52.212-2, Evaluation � Commercial Items;- - FAR 52.212-3 ALT 1 � Offeror Representations and Certifications � Commercial Items Alternate 1 - FAR 52.212-4, Contract Terms and Conditions--Commercial Items; -The following DFARS clauses apply to this solicitation: 252.204-7008, Compliance with Safeguarding Covered Defense Information Controls 252.204- 7009, Limitations on the Use or Disclosure of Third-Party Contractor Reported Cyber Incident Information 252.204-7012, Safeguarding Covered Defense Information and Cyber Incident Reporting 252.204-7015, Notice of Authorized Disclosure of Information for Litigation Support 252.204-7018, Prohibition on the Acquisition of Covered Defense Telecommunications Equipment or Services apply to this solicitation. 252.204-7021, Contractor Compliance with the Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Level Requirements. 252.204-7025, Notice of Cybersecurity Maturity Model Certification Level Requirements. Full text of incorporated FAR/DFARS clauses and provisions are may be accessed electronically at https://acquisition.gov/far/ and https://www.acq.osd.mil/dpap/dars/dfarspgi/current/index.html. The use in this solicitation of any Federal Acquisition Regulation (48 CFR Chapter 1) clause with an authorized deviation is indicated by the addition of �(Deviation)� after the date of the clause. Additional Terms and Conditions: In accordance with DFARS Clause 252.211-7003, the contractor shall provide a unique item identifier (IUD) for all delivered items for which the Government�s unit acquisition cost is $5,000 or more. Payment will be via Wide Area Workflow (WAWF) within the Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE). This solicitation requires an active registration with the System for Award Management (SAM) prior to award, pursuant to applicable regulations and guidelines. Registration information can be found at www.sam.gov. For information on this acquisition contact Jennifer Vatousiou at jennifer.m.vatousiou.civ@us.navy.mil. SOLE SOURCE SPECIFICATION: NATSC uses specialized electrostatic discharge (ESD) benches to repair and test the modules. These modules are required to be placed on ESD benches to prevent electrostatic discharge from disrupting the internal electronic components during maintenance, as well as to protect integrated components that do not need to be removed. Due to the length of these modules, benches must be specific lengths to prevent the equipment from hanging off the edges and sustaining unnecessary damage. It is critical to ensure that these benches continue to be fully functional. NATSC relocated its operations with benches that were purchased from Workplace Modular Systems Inc. Since establishing operations at the current station, all subsequent bench acquisitions have been sourced from Workplace Modular Systems Inc. This vendor provides custom-built benches with ESD resistors already integrated, offering the capability to mate with existing units and be reconfigured as the facility workflow requires. The existing benches have gone through testing proving they can withstand the harsh chemicals used on them daily. These benches have also been proven to remain within ESD specifications even when modified with additional holes to support the jigs, tools, and fixtures required during repair and testing. Due to the age of the ESD benches and their constant use, it has been determined that refurbishing the existing benches would be the most cost-effective way to maintain them, rather than purchasing new benches. As Workplace Modular Systems Inc. manufactured all the benches currently located at the facility, they are the only company that can provide the necessary parts for refurbishment. The alternative to refurbishing all the ESD benches is to purchase entirely new ESD benches from either Workplace Modular Systems Inc. or from an alternate vendor. Purchasing all new benches from the original manufacturer would require a lead time of several months to acquire the hundreds of benches slated for replacement, and this path does not include the additional logistical effort of removing, disposing of, and installing the hardware. Additionally, introducing a brand-new model of bench would require first article testing and facilities inspections to ensure that all electrical connections are within code, which may necessitate structural and electrical modifications to the facility to accommodate the new ESD specifications. On top of those requirements, new jigs, tools, and fixtures designed specifically to support and keep the new benches operational would need to be acquired and stored. The additional overhead of testing, inspecting, modifying the facility, and procuring new fixtures would introduce significant extra costs and result in the workstations being unusable for a substantial period of business days. This option also does not account for the baseline effort required to remove, dispose of, and install the benches. Based on the above, it is not reasonable to conclude the potential savings from competition can offset the significant duplicative cost and schedule and mission impact associated with purchasing a different brand product. Therefore, it is in the best interest of the Government to solicit and award this requirement on a sole source only basis.

title: Large Area Display System (LADS)
description: Sources Sought Notice Number: H9224126S61892 The Technology Application Program Office (TAPO) is conducting market research to identify potential vendors capable of responding to the requirements described below. However, it should be noted that information gathered through this notice may significantly influence the Government�s acquisition strategy. All interested parties will be required to respond separately to any solicitations posted as a result of this sources sought notice. Requirements: The Government seeks to identify potential sources with aircraft Large Area Display System (LADS) for military rotary wing Air Vehicle Systems (AVS) that are commercial products. These airborne avionics grade display system will serve as the primary human machine interface for pilotage and situational awareness tasks by the aircrew. Safety-critical video processing and control are expected to reside externally to the LADS. The Government is interested in a display subsystem capable of deterministic, bounded-latency presentation of video and symbology as an endpoint within an existing Cockpit Display System architecture. The system must be designed with a Modular Open Systems Approach (MOSA) to ensure interoperability, reusability, and future growth. Attributes of interest are Size, Weight, and Power (SWaP), environmental and electromagnetic susceptibility characteristics, and display characteristics. Further details are available to potential sources that the Joint Certification Program (JCP) have certified as eligible for access to unclassified, non-public military technical data and have a current JCP approved DD Form 2345, Military Critical Technical Data Agreement. Interested sources may recommend other NAICS Codes for consideration. Small Business Size Standard: The small business size standard is 1,350 employees. PSC: 1680 - Miscellaneous aircraft accessories and components. B. FAA Technical Standard Order authorization, if any (TSO number and revision). C. Rotary wing installations under a Type Certificate or Supplemental Type Certificate, if any (TC/STC number, aircraft make and model, approximate units fielded). 4. Small Business Considerations A. Whether the respondent is the manufacturer of the LADS. If not, ability to comply with the nonmanufacturer rule. B. Ability to comply with the applicable limitation on subcontracting. 5. title: Gestione globale del centro socio assistenziale San Michele di Entracque.
description: L’appalto ha per oggetto l’affidamento del servizio di gestione della struttura per anziani denominata “Centro socio assistenziale San Michele”, che costituisce la parte preponderante del contratto, oltre ai seguenti servizi integrativi: – fornitura del servizio infermieristico alla popolazione residente; – fornitura di bagni protetti agli anziani richiedenti; – fornitura di pasti da erogare a domicilio agli anziani richiedenti; – fornitura di pasti da erogare agli utenti della mensa scolastica comunale; – assistenza agli alunni trasportati sullo scuolabus comunale; – assistenza agli alunni frequentanti la mensa scolastica comunale; – pulizia locali indicati dal Comune, ambulatorio infermieristico; – servizi aggiuntivi a richiesta e discrezione del Comune. Il Centro socio assistenziale “San Michele” è una struttura di proprietà comunale, sita a Entracque in via Ospedale n. 72, nel centro del paese, ubicata in un edificio storico, un tempo utilizzato come Ospedale di carità e Ospizio. La sede è stata oggetto di ristrutturazione edilizia, di riqualificazione e di efficientamento energetico negli anni 2024-2026. La struttura, che permette un’ospitalità permanente, risulta in possesso delle autorizzazioni necessarie al funzionamento finalizzato alla “Progettazione ed erogazione di servizi socio-sanitari ed assistenziali rivolti ad anziani autosufficienti e non autosufficienti in regime di residenzialità”. Le caratteristiche della struttura e della gestione sono specificate nel progetto per l'affidamento della gestione globale del centro socio assistenziale "San Michele" approvato con deliberazione di Giunta del Comune di Entracque n. 52 del 24/06/2026; con deliberazione di Giunta del Comune di Entracque n. 64 del 26/08/2026 è stata invece approvata la versione aggiornata del quadro economico.

title: Manchester International Airport - OLE Phase 3 Works
description: The planned introduction of longer train services to the Airport in response to future demand growth will mean that double stacking arrangements of trains as currently used will no longer be viable. Through the project's Delivery Steering Group, Northern and TransPennine Express have carried out analysis which has identified that additional platform capacity is needed at the airport in order to realise the full benefit of longer train services serving the airport. The scheme is part of a package of proposed measures in the Manchester area that are being designed/planned to boost capacity and resilience, emanating from the Cross Manchester Capacity and Reliability Improvement Study. Improving the operation of train services in the centre of Manchester and providing further capacity at Manchester Airport station, aligns with the strategic aims of Network Rail, TfGM, TfN and the wider industry. This project in in Tranche 1 of the Manchester and North West Transformation Programme (MNTP): A remodelling of the station at Manchester Airport, specifically a platform addition or extension of multiple platforms, or provision of a new turnback facility, will be essential to accommodate the planned implementation of longer rolling stock services. The redevelopment of these platforms will enable permissive working of two 6x24m (144m) trains, in two of the four platforms at the Airport Station. This will allow for the unaltered retention of all existing TOC services both originating and terminating at the Airport Station under 'double-stacking' conditions. The scope areas for this package are as follows: - OLE Specialist Works for Manchester Airport Station Remodelling

The Bureau of International Narcotics and Law Enforcement Affairs (INL) is an instrumental leader in the development of policies and programs to combat international narcotics and crime. INL programs support two of the Department of State's strategic goals: (1) to reduce the entry of illegal drugs and migrants into the United States; and (2) to minimize the impact of international crime on the United States and its citizens. One of the many ways to meet these goals is to partner with allied governments to promote the modernization of, and support the enforcement operations of, their foreign criminal justice systems and law enforcement agencies. INL assists host nations with the construction and rehabilitation of facilities that enable those nations to enhance their capacity to manage security incidents within their own countries. In cooperation with the Government of Honduras, INL is providing technical assistance for the rehabilitation and improvement of the FEN Puerto Castilla facility � an active operational base supporting maritime security, interdiction, and emergency response activities. The existing infrastructure requires comprehensive rehabilitation to support safe, reliable operations and compliance with applicable building codes and mission requirements. End-user transfer. The completed facilities and all equipment furnished under this contract are provided as assistance to the Government of Honduras and will be transferred to the Fuerza Especial Naval upon final acceptance. The Contractor shall deliver all warranty documentation, operations and maintenance manuals, and training in a form usable by the end user. Existing infrastructure at the site comprises a timber dock supported by preserved timber piles; an open-sided steel-framed structure with concrete slab-on-grade and metal roof housing the workshop and barracks areas; and existing electrical and utility services serving the facility. All works shall be integrated into the existing infrastructure with minimal disruption and without modification to primary structural systems unless expressly stated in this SOW. This project consolidates three interrelated sub-projects into a single design-build procurement: Rehabilitation of approximately 40 linear meters of the existing maritime dock (superstructure replacement, retaining existing piles) and construction of a new 15-linear-meter dock extension (new piles and full structure), with an optional concrete topping slab system over the full 55 m of dock surface; Construction and improvement of an Outboard Engine Workshop (approximately 80 m�), including enclosures, access elements, cladding, electrical, plumbing, ventilation, and fire protection; Construction and improvement of Emergency Response Barracks (approximately 40 m�, dormitory for eight personnel), including enclosures, finishes, suspended ceiling, doors, windows, electrical, and life safety provisions. title: Sources Sought - SLDA NCSO
description: This is a Sources Sought Notice for market research purposes only to identify capable firms for on-site Nuclear Criticality Safety (NCS) support for the Shallow Land Disposal Area (SLDA) environmental-remediation project in Parks Township, Armstrong County, Pennsylvania. This is a special notice only. No proposals are being requested or accepted in response to this notice. All responses must be submitted electronically through the designated Market Survey Form. 1. Description of Work The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Buffalo District, is seeking capability statements from qualified firms to determine the availability and technical capability of firms able to provide independent on-site nuclear criticality safety support for the Formerly Utilized Sites Remedial Action Program (FUSRAP) SLDA project. The anticipated requirement is a firm-fixed-price service contract with cost-reimbursable travel, consisting of a one-year base period and four option years. The contractor will provide a qualified primary NCS Officer and alternate NCS Officer to support active environmental-remediation operations at the SLDA site. The contractor will serve as an independent technical advisor to USACE and will provide oversight and quality assurance of the remediation contractor�s NCS program. The anticipated scope includes: Providing on-site presence during active remediation operations. Conducting field walkdowns and direct observation of remediation activities. Reviewing Nuclear Criticality Safety Evaluations, calculations, technical-basis documents, work plans, procedures, and other submittals. Assessing the implementation and effectiveness of criticality-safety controls. Conducting audits, assessments, and surveillance of the remediation contractor�s NCS program. Reviewing safety, radiological, operational, and nuclear quality-assurance documentation. Supporting the safe handling, measurement, processing, storage, transport, and disposal of excavated radiological materials, including special nuclear material. Preparing independent technical reports identifying findings, risks, and recommended corrective actions. Supporting coordination with USACE, the site owner, regulators, and other project stakeholders, as required. The work will primarily occur at the SLDA site in Parks Township, Pennsylvania. The requirement may also include periodic travel to USACE offices and other off-site meeting locations. 2. The Government is not obligated to issue a solicitation or award a contract as a result of this notice. AGENCY INFORMATION Department of the Interior National Park Service Contracting Operations (ConOps) East Point of Contact: Edward Dingle, Jr. Edward_dingle@ios.doi.gov 3. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT The Department of the Interior, National Park Service (NPS), is conducting market research to determine the availability and capability of qualified construction contractors to perform the Atrium Replacement at the Chickamauga Visitor Center, Chickamauga and Chattanooga National Military Park, Fort Oglethorpe, Georgia, Project CHCH 315696. The contemplated project generally consists of replacement of the existing Visitor Center atrium, limited parking-lot modifications, reconfiguration of the north and south plazas, and associated fire-protection, plumbing, mechanical, electrical, communications, fire-alarm, architectural, structural, civil/site, and landscape improvements. The work is anticipated to be performed under a single prime construction contract and includes multiple interdependent construction disciplines requiring significant coordination by the prime contractor. Major elements of work include, but are not necessarily limited to: � Selective demolition and demolition of the existing Visitor Center atrium. � Construction of the replacement atrium, including structural, architectural, roofing, building-envelope, curtain-wall/glazing, entrance, and interior-finish work. � Civil, landscape, parking, pedestrian pathway, paving, grading, earthwork, stormwater, and related site improvements. � Fire-protection modifications, including dry-pipe sprinkler-system work. � Plumbing and facility drainage improvements. � HVAC/mechanical modifications, including associated piping, ductwork, equipment, controls, supports, vibration/seismic requirements, and testing and balancing. � Electrical modifications, including demolition, conductors, raceways, grounding, panelboards, wiring devices, lighting, and associated electrical distribution work. � Fire-alarm, communications, and related life-safety systems. � Temporary facilities and controls, environmental protection, construction waste management, testing, commissioning, project documentation, and closeout. The specifications separately identify contract line items covering site demolition, demolition of the existing Visitor Center atrium, civil and landscape improvements, construction of the new atrium, fire-sprinkler upgrades, plumbing/drainage upgrades, mechanical improvements, and electrical improvements. Occupied Facility and Public Access The work will occur at an active National Park Service visitor facility. Areas outside the construction limits are expected to remain occupied by NPS personnel and accessible to park visitors. Construction activities must therefore be planned and coordinated to protect employees and the public, maintain access and required exits, and minimize disruption to park and Visitor Center operations. Temporary construction controls include fencing, barriers, and separation of construction activities from occupied/public areas. The project also contains requirements concerning historic-preservation treatment, protection of existing resources, ground-disturbing activities, construction scheduling, quality control, environmental protection, fire/life-safety continuity, and multidisciplinary construction coordination. Accordingly, the Government is particularly interested in determining whether firms�especially qualified small businesses�possess the experience, personnel, subcontractor resources, bonding capacity, and management systems necessary to serve as the prime contractor and integrator for the complete multidisciplinary requirement. 4. title: TRAINING AND SUPPORT SERVICES FOR THE INTAC PROGRAM OFFICE
description: SOURCES SOUGHT ANNOUNCEMENT � FOR INFORMATION ONLY Individual Terrorism Awareness Course (INTAC) 1. Introduction: This is a Sources Sought market survey for informational and planning purposes only, in accordance with the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 10. No proposals are being requested or accepted with this announcement. The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) � UMSB Contracting is conducting market research for the follow-on contract to support the Individual Terrorism Awareness Course (INTAC). The purpose is to identify parties who may be interested in and capable of performing this requirement. 2. Background: The INTAC program is a comprehensive, professional, resident training course that enhances the antiterrorism and force protection awareness posture of U.S. Army, Department of War (DoW), and other U.S. Government personnel. The course consists of a combination of classroom lectures and hands-on, performance-based training modules designed to provide realistic and challenging scenarios based on past events and current intelligence. The training prepares personnel who are considered to be at a medium-to-high risk from terrorism or criminal activity for their official travel and duties outside the Continental United States (OCONUS). 3. Requirement: The Contractor shall be required to provide all labor, equipment, materials, supervision, and contiguous training facilities necessary to conduct the INTAC training sessions and associated training modules. The core INTAC training is a multi-day session, supplemented by various optional modules that can be ordered as needed. See attached the DRAFT PWS. The Contractor will be responsible for providing and maintaining all necessary facilities, including road courses with varied configurations, firearms ranges, non-lethal shooting facilities, classrooms, and administrative and storage space for Government-furnished property. 4. Proposed Contract: The proposed contract is anticipated to be a Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) Single Award Task Order Contract (SATOC) with a five-year ordering period. The estimated contract ceiling is approximately $10,000,000. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 611519, �Other Technical and Trade Schools,� with a size standard of $16.5 million. All business sizes are welcome to respond; however, small business vendors are highly encouraged. 5. Requested Information: Interested parties are requested to submit a capability package that is not a proposal but a statement regarding the company's existing experience and capabilities. Please include the following in your response: Organization name, physical address, CAGE Code, and Unique Entity ID. Socioeconomic Status (e.g., Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business, etc.). A summary of your company's capability to perform and manage a contract of this scope and complexity. Include 3 examples of comparable work performed within the past five years, with a brief description, customer name(s) and contact information, and the dollar value. A description of the resources and personnel your company possesses to perform this work as the prime contractor. Discuss any services that would be subcontracted and the technical capabilities of those subcontractors. Your company�s current facility clearance status. Provide comments to the attached DRAFT PWS. 6. Specific Questions: In addition to the general information requested above, please provide detailed responses to the following questions. These responses will help us better understand your capabilities in relation to the specific needs of the INTAC program. Range and Type of Classes: Describe your experience providing a diverse range of training courses similar to those in the INTAC program, from basic firearms and driving to advanced modules like Tactical Combat Casualty Care (TCCC) and Vehicle Commandeering. How do you ensure curriculum remains current with evolving threats? Facilities and Environment: Detail your existing training facilities. Specifically address your capacity to provide multiple road courses (paved, unimproved, off-road), skid pads, varied firearms ranges (including "drive-and-shoot" ranges), and indoor non-lethal training areas that can be configured for realistic scenarios, all within 125 miles of the Pentagon. Instructor Training and Qualifications: What are your minimum qualifications and certification standards for instructors across the different training disciplines (driving, firearms, medical)? Describe your process for recruiting, training, and continuously evaluating instructors to ensure they are experts in their respective fields. Scalability of Classes: Explain your capability to provide a flexible and scalable training schedule. How would you accommodate both the core INTAC course for up to 30 students and concurrently offer smaller, specialized training modules for groups as small as 1-3 students on an as-needed basis? 7. Submission Details: This market survey is for informational and planning purposes only and does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP). The Government will not award a contract based on this announcement. Interested companies shall respond to this Sources Sought synopsis no later than 1:00 P.M. ET on 9 October 2026 to Giorgiana Chen at Giorgiana.Chen@usace.army.mil and Douglas Pohlman, at Douglas.E.Pohlman@usace.army.mil. RFI questions are due by 1:00 P.M. ET on 18 September 2026.

title: Y1DA--Women's Health Center (Minor) Construction - Albany - Project 528-812
description: SYNOPSIS: INTRODUCTION: In accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 10.002(b)(2), this Sources Sought Notice is for market research and information purposes only at this time and shall not be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation on the part of the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA). The Department of Veterans Affairs, Veterans Health Administration (VHA), Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) is conducting a market survey and is seeking potential sources for the Women's Health Center (Minor) Construction project at the Albany VA Medical Center (VAMC) located at 113 Holland Ave., Albany, NY 12208. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The Albany VAMC is seeking a general contractor to construct a new standalone two-story 13,000 square foot building for the new Women s Health Center that will house dedicated primary care, mental health care, imaging, and additional specialty services, separate from the main hospital. PROCUREMENT INFORMATION: The proposed project will be a competitive firm-fixed-price contract utilizing the design-bid-build approach (Final Specifications and Drawings will be provided). The anticipated solicitation will be issued as either a Request for Proposal (RFP) in accordance with FAR Part 15, considering Technical and Price Factors or as an Invitation for Bid (IFB) in accordance with FAR Part 14. The results and analysis of the market research will finalize the determination of the procurement method. The type of socio-economic set-aside, if any, will depend upon the responses to this notice and any other information gathered during the market research process. This project is planned for advertising in late November 2026. In accordance with VAAR 836.204, the magnitude of construction is between $10,000,000.00 and $20,000,000.00. The applicable North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 236220 with a size standard of $45 million. The duration of the project is currently estimated at 730 calendar days from the issuance of a Notice to Proceed. The services for this project will include providing all construction related services such as: providing labor, materials and equipment required to complete the project as per contract documents prepared by an independent Architect-Engineer firm. The results and analysis of the market research will determine whether to limit competition among the small business categories, proceed with full and open competition as other than small business, or use a tiered set-aside evaluation. The type of socioeconomic set-aside, if any, will depend upon the responses to this notice and any other information gathered during the market research process. All socioeconomic categories are encouraged to respond to this announcement. CAPABILITY STATEMENT: Respondents shall provide a general capabilities statement to include the following information: Section 1: Provide company name, Unique Entity Identifier number associate with SAM.gov, company address, Point-of-Contact name, phone number and email. Section 2: Provide company business size based on NAICS code 236220. Also, provide business type (i.e., Large Business, Small Business, Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, Small Disadvantaged Business, Women-Owned Small Business, Hub Zone Small Business, etc.). Section 3: Provide a Statement of Interest in the project. Section 4: Provide the prime contractor s available bonding capacity in the form of a letter of intent from your bonding company with this submission. Section 5: Provide the type of work your company has performed in the past in support of the same or similar requirement. This section is IMPORTANT as it will help to determine the type of socio-economic set-aside, if any. Please provide the following in your response: No more than three (3) contracts that your company has performed within the last seven (7) years that are of comparable size, complexity, and scope to this requirement. Include the project name, project owner and contact information as this person may be contacted for further information, project scope, project size (Example: square footage), building use (Example: Medical Facility, Office Building, etc.), project dollar value, start and completion dates. Provide specific examples that relate aspects of previous projects to the proposed project. Describe specific technical skills and key personnel your company possess to perform the requirements described under description of work. Describe your Self-Performed** effort (as either a Prime or Subcontractor). Describe Self-Performed work in terms of dollar value and description. **Self-Performed means work performed by the offeror themselves, NOT work performed by another company for them for any of the project examples provided. It is requested that interested contractors submit a response (electronic submission) of no more than eight (8) single sided pages, single-spaced, 12-point font minimum that addresses the above information. This response must be submitted as a single application-generated (not scanned) PDF document that is less than or equal to 4MB in size. Please note that hard copies will not be accepted. Please also include a cover page, which includes, at a minimum: the company s name, address, Dun & Bradstreet number, socio-economic status, point-of-contact name, phone number, and e-mail address. Responses must include the Sources Sought number and project title in the subject line of their e-mail response. Submissions (responses) shall be submitted via email to the primary point of contact listed below by October 9, 2026 at 1:00 PM ET. No phone calls will be accepted. The Capabilities Statement submitted in response to this Sources Sought shall not be considered to be a bid or proposal. This notice is for information and planning purposes only and is neither to be construed as a commitment by the Government nor will the Government pay for information solicited. No evaluation letters and/or results will be issued to the respondents. After completing its analyses, the Government will determine whether to limit competition among the small business categories listed above or proceed with full and open competition as other than small business. At this time no solicitation exists; therefore, please DO NOT REQUEST A COPY OF THE SOLICITATION. If a solicitation is released it will be synopsized in Contract Opportunities at https://Sam.gov. It is the potential offeror's responsibility to monitor this site for the release of any solicitation or synopsis. title: Rockaway Contract 3, ADA Cross Over, Queens County, New York
description: Pre-Solicitation NoticeThe New York District, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (District) is preparing plans and specifications for construction of the Rockaway Contract 3 ADA cross over. DESCRIPTION: The East Rockaway Inlet to Rockaway Inlet (or Rockaway) project area is in the Borough of Queens, New York City. The Atlantic Oceanfront shoreline, which is a peninsula approximately 10 miles in length, generally referred to as the Rockaways, separates the Atlantic Ocean from Jamaica Bay immediately to the north. This project, Rockaway Contract 3, includes the following: nine elevated, timber, pedestrian crossover structures that will provide ADA access to the beach, sand fence and dune vegetation will be added to the localized areas of the ADA structures. The nine ADA elevated timber crossovers are located at Beach 147th, 142nd, 135th, 131st, 67th, 44th, 17th, 13th and 11th streets. The span of the truss deck is approximately 44 feet over the crest of the dune and has landward and seaward ramps varying in length. There are also options for aluminum railings and handrails and reinforced plastic lumber decking, as well as options to remove 19 timber groins. Award is projected in November/December 2026. Estimated project duration is 18 months about 550 calendar days. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 237990 (Other Heavy and Civil Engineering Construction).LOCATION: The project area is in the Borough of Queens, New York City.Construction cost is in the range of $10,000,000 to $25,000,000.

title: Market Survey - Microgrid - United States Army Garrison (USAG) Ansbach; Bavaria, Germany � Katterbach Kaserne
description: A market survey is being conducted to determine if there are a reasonable number of interested businesses for the below future project. If your firm is an Other than Small, Small Business, certified HUBZone, 8A, Woman-Owned Small Business or Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business and you are interested in this project please respond appropriately. Project Location: United States Army Garrison (USAG) Ansbach; Bavaria, Germany � Katterbach Kaserne Project Description: This is a Design/Bid/Build project. The US Government intends to solicit to construction firms to perform military construction and other Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (SRM) projects in the country of Germany as described within this announcement for the state of Bavaria. Construct a fully functional, islandable, and black start capable microgrid. The microgrid will include solar photovoltaic (PV) power production to provide daily, on-site renewable energy generation to offset incoming power from the local utility. Additionally, this project will also include diesel fuel generators, a battery energy storage system (BESS), and a microgrid controller to control all energy generation assets and manage electrical loads. This microgrid system will connect and distribute power on a government owned electrical distribution system. This microgrid is to provide resilient power to facilities at Katterbach/Bismarck Kaserne. Contract duration is estimated at 743 calendar days. The estimated cost range is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. NAICS code is 237130. All interested Other than Small, Small Business, certified HUBZONE, 8A, Woman-Owned Small Business or Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business contractors should respond to this survey via the form link or QR code provided on this posting by Friday, October 09, 2026 by 2:00 PM Eastern Time. Responses should include: Identification and verification of the company�s size status. Contractor�s Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE Code(s). Identification of firm�s current single and aggregate performance and payment bond limits. Submissions of Past Performance from affiliates shall include documentation of the affiliation to the offeror. To be relevant, the projects submitted should be greater than 95% construction complete or completed within the last five (5) years and are similar to this project in scope and complexity. Demonstrate experience including self-performing 15% of the construction. Provide documentation demonstrating experience for projects of similar type projects. Each project must include the name, title, project role, e-mail address, and telephone number of at least one reference. References may be used to verify project size, scope, dollar value, percentages and quality of performance. Projects similar in scope shall include construction of a microgrid demonstrating a sufficient combination of the following scope elements to substantiate the offeror's technical competency, based on the complexity, scale, and integration of the demonstrated elements: (1) Installation of diesel centralized generators to power multiple buildings and fuel tank farm system (2) Installation of necessary breakers and switchgears (3) Installation of photovoltaic systems (4) Installation of electrical and telecommunication duct bank (5) Installation of a BESS (Battery Energy Storage System) (6) Information and communication systems (7)Commissioning of microgrid systems Projects similar in size to this project include: Construction of microgrid systems that meet or exceed the following: (1) Construction and installation of diesel generators able to handle loads of .5 to 2.5MW (2) Construction and installation of a PV Array of power production of 500 kW to 1.5 MW (3) Construction and installation of a BESS of 2 MWh to 10 MWh Based on definitions above, for each project submitted include: (1) Current percentage of construction complete and the date when it was or will be completed. title: CRANE AND HOIST REPAIRS - WASHINGTON AQUEDUCT
description: The purpose of this special notice is to issue notice of intent to restrict competition for certain commercial services under the simplified acquisition threshold. The Washington Aqueduct has a requirement for the procurement of critical repairs for the several crane and hoist systems located at the WA facilities. These repairs were specifically identified during the annual inspection required to maintain safety standards for safe operation in accordance with OSHA and USACE EM 385-1-1 regulations, as well as ASME/ANSI B30 Crane Standard Codes. Authority to Restrict Competition: Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO), Subpart 12.102(a).Reason for Authority Cited: RFO 12.102(a) allows the Contracting Officer (KO) to restrict competition when procuring commercial products or services under the Simplified Acquisition Threshold (SAT) when they determine that only one source is reasonably available to fulfill the requirement. The Government requires critical repairs to its crane and hoist systems to support the Washington Aqueducts potable water treatment program. The proposed source, American Mergers AND Manufacturing International LLC (dba Waymaker), is the contractor currently performing the Crane Inspection and Maintenance Service Contract. Under this contract, Waymaker performed the comprehensive annual inspection that identified the required repairs. Because Waymaker performed this highly detailed inspection, they possess direct working knowledge of the specific repairs needed and the precise parts required. Procuring repairs from a new contractor would result in unacceptable delays and inflated costs due to the need for duplicate re-inspections. Because no other contractor has this immediate, intimate knowledge of the specific deficiencies, it is determined that only one source is reasonably available to perform these commercial services.

title: GEN6 V006 CYBER SCAN
description: The Naval Air Warfare Center Aircraft Division (NAWCAD), Patuxent River, MD intends to negotiate and award a Delivery Order under Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) N0042126G1005 with Collins Aerospace (CA), 400 Collins Road NE, Cedar Rapids, IA 52498-0505 to provide Naval Air Systems Command, Air Combat Electronics Program Office (PMA209) with the GEN6 V006 Cyber Scan in support of the AN/ARC-210(V) RT-2036(C) v006, hereinafter referred to as Gen6. This effort consists of the following elements: Develop one (1) beta software scan of the Gen6 v006. Develop one (1) final software scan of the Gen6 v006. This acquisition is being pursued on a sole-source basis under the authority of 10 U.S.C 2304(c)(1), as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 6.103-2, �only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements.� The AN/ARC-210(V) electronic protection (EP) radio systems and associated support equipment have been determined to be commercial products and CA will not provide or sell the technical data necessary to procure the items competitively or provide support for these products. Therefore, CA is the only responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements. THIS NOTICE OF INTENT IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSALS. title: Microgrid - United States Army Garrison (USAG) Ansbach; Bavaria, Germany � Katterbach Kaserne
description: A market survey is being conducted to determine if there are a reasonable number of interested businesses for the below future project. If your firm is an Other than Small, Small Business, certified HUBZone, 8A, Woman-Owned Small Business or Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business and you are interested in this project please respond appropriately. Project Location: United States Army Garrison (USAG) Ansbach; Bavaria, Germany � Katterbach Kaserne Project Description: This is a Design/Bid/Build project. The US Government intends to solicit to construction firms to perform military construction and other Sustainment, Restoration, and Modernization (SRM) projects in the country of Germany as described within this announcement for the state of Bavaria. Construct a fully functional, islandable, and black start capable microgrid. The microgrid will include solar photovoltaic (PV) power production to provide daily, on-site renewable energy generation to offset incoming power from the local utility. Additionally, this project will also include diesel fuel generators, a battery energy storage system (BESS), and a microgrid controller to control all energy generation assets and manage electrical loads. This microgrid system will connect and distribute power on a government owned electrical distribution system. This microgrid is to provide resilient power to facilities at Katterbach/Bismarck Kaserne. Contract duration is estimated at 743 calendar days. The estimated cost range is between $25,000,000 and $100,000,000. NAICS code is 237130. All interested Other than Small, Small Business, certified HUBZONE, 8A, Woman-Owned Small Business or Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business contractors should respond to this survey via the form link or QR code provided on this posting by Friday, October 09, 2026 by 2:00 PM Eastern Time. Responses should include: Identification and verification of the company�s size status. Contractor�s Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and CAGE Code(s). Identification of firm�s current single and aggregate performance and payment bond limits. Description of Experience � Provide descriptions on up to three (3) projects completed by you as the prime contractor or if the offeror is a Small Business, they can provide Past Performance of affiliates in accordance with DFARS 215.305(a)(2)(C). Submissions of Past Performance from affiliates shall include documentation of the affiliation to the offeror. To be relevant, the projects submitted should be greater than 95% construction complete or completed within the last five (5) years and are similar to this project in scope and complexity. Demonstrate experience including self-performing 15% of the construction. Provide documentation demonstrating experience for projects of similar type projects. Each project must include the name, title, project role, e-mail address, and telephone number of at least one reference. References may be used to verify project size, scope, dollar value, percentages and quality of performance. Projects similar in scope shall include construction of a microgrid demonstrating a majority of the following scope elements: (1) Installation of diesel centralized generators to power multiple buildings and fuel tank farm system (2) Installation of necessary breakers and switchgears (3) Installation of photovoltaic systems (4) Installation of electrical and telecommunication duct bank (5) Installation of a BESS (Battery Energy Storage System) (6) Information and communication systems (7)Commissioning of microgrid systems Projects similar in size to this project include: Construction of microgrid systems that meet or exceed the following: (1) Construction and installation of diesel generators able to handle loads of .5 to 2.5MW (2) Construction and installation of a PV Array of power production of 500 kW to 1.5 MW (3) Construction and installation of a BESS of 2 MWh to 10 MWh Based on definitions above, for each project submitted include: (1) Current percentage of construction complete and the date when it was or will be completed. (2) Size of the project (3) Scope of the project (4) The dollar value of the construction contract (5) The percentage of work that was self-performed as project and/or construction management services or physical construction type work. (6) Whether the project was design build or design/bid/build (7) Identify the number of subcontractors by construction trade utilized for each project. 5. title: GLWACH Construct Hospital Parking and Renovate Optical Fabrication Laboratory (OFL)
description: W912DQ279A002 REQUEST FOR MARKET INFORMATION / NOTICE OF INDUSTRY WEBINAR FOR GENERAL LEONARD WOOD ARMY COMMUNITY HOSPTIAL (GLWACH) CONSTRUCT HOSPITAL PARKING AND RENOVATE OPTICAL FABRICATION LABORATORY (OFL) PURPOSE: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Kansas City District, is requesting market intelligence information to identify qualified industry partners capable of supporting a potential Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a for the stated General Leonard Wood Community Hospital (GLWACH) project at Fort Leonard Wood, MO. The Government is seeking industry feedback to better understand the commercial market interest, market capabilities, market capacity and innovative business practices that may inform the acquisition strategy and structure of the potential OT Agreement. This is not a Request for Qualifications. It does not constitute a commitment by the Government to award an agreement or reimburse respondents for costs associated with responding. Participation is voluntary. PROJECT OVERVIEW and REQUIREMENTS: Project Title: Hospital Parking Lot Construction and Optical Fabrication Laboratory (OFL) Renovation Location: Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri Agency: USACE, Kansas City District (NWK) NAICS Code: 236220-Commerical and Industrial Building Construction Planning and design activities are ongoing. The project�s phased funding profile is listed below: FY23: $31M (Expires September 30, 2027) FY29: $35M (Anticipated) The estimated magnitude for the entire overall effort is between $40 Million and $60M. The new General Leonard Wood Army Community Hospital requires the construction of new hospital parking lots, the renovation of an Optical Fabrication Laboratory (OFL), site work and infrastructure to support the newly constructed GLWACH. The parking lot construction includes site grading and drainage, vehicle circulation roads and parking, pedestrian sidewalks, landscaping (including the planting of trees), site lighting, wayfinding, and video surveillance. The contractor must always maintain 970 parking stalls during construction. The contractor must also ensure safe pedestrian access from the existing parking lots to the new hospital. A construction phasing plan and traffic management plan must be implemented to maintain a safe environment for hospital patrons and staff. The OFL renovation includes the demolition and replacement of the west wall at the current mechanical, electrical, plumbing (MEP) room, removing all equipment inside the MEP and capping all roof penetrations. After demolition the MEP space will remain and become additional storage space for the OFL contract. A new ADA (American with Disabilities Act) compliant entrance vestibule be provided on the west side of the building where the old connection to the hospital was. The OFL also includes the renovation of a medical supply warehouse. To meet life safety codes the optical fabrication lab (OFL) space on the lower level will receive a new egress corridor and lightning protection. The facility must remain fully operational during all deconstruction, demolition, and construction efforts. The former General Leonard Army Community Hospital and infrastructure must be decommissioned, dismantled, demolished, and removed prior to the construction of the new parking lot. This work included the decommissioning of a hospital and clinic, a central utility plant, abatement of hazardous materials and environmental liabilities. All existing paving, utilities, and other site appurtenances, including a helipad, must also be demolished and removed. Approximately 60,000 to 70,000 cubic yards of excavated soil will need to be cut and transported from an adjacent location to the project site for fill. POTENTIAL DELIVERY APPROACH: The Government is evaluating execution of this project using a Construction Manager At Risk (CMAR) Other Transaction Agreement authorized under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a with USACE as the Designer of Record (DOR). Using CMAR OT, the Government is particularly interested in commercial and collaborative practices to determine the following: Phasing and execution strategies to efficiently deliver the project Construction packaging and execution to optimize the given phased funding profile Early and continuous Government-industry collaboration; Collaborative design development and constructability; Contractor-Government open-book cost estimating and cost transparency; Collaborative project phasing and schedule certainty; Collaborative risk identification, mitigation and allocation; Innovation and alternative construction techniques; Overall cost, schedule, and mission outcomes. INDUSTRY INFORMATION REQUESTED: This request is the Government's primary mechanism for obtaining detailed market intelligence regarding industry interest, capability and capacity, relevant experience using CMAR, open-book pricing, and potential commercial practices. The Government welcomes candid industry feedback and recommendations regarding the use the same or similar collaborative commercial practices, agreement terms, project phasing, risk sharing, governance, pricing approaches, and other considerations that could improve successful execution of this project using CMAR under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Interested firms should complete and submit: The attached Market Intelligence Questionnaire and A summary of their interest and capabilities to perform all the work identified for this project. The summary interest and capabilities is not a formal Request for Qualifications, and the response should not exceed 10 pages in length. The summary should also include the following information: The Company information (name, address, contact information, business structure) Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code and/or Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and SAM.gov registration, if available. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS: Please submit the completed attached questionnaire and a summary of interest and capabilities via email to the individuals listed below no later than: 2:00 p.m. Central Time, 9 October 2026. Jeri L. Halterman at Jeri.l.halterman@usace.army.mil Courtesy copy: Dave Walsh at david.j.walsh@usace.army.mil Interested firms are encouraged to add themselves to the Interested Vendors List associated with this announcement on SAM.gov to receive future updates. INDUSTRY WEBINAR: A virtual Industry Day to better explain the project requirements is scheduled prior to the requested date of submission, Wednesday, September 23, 2026, starting at 2:00 p.m. Central Daylight Time. Please email Jeri L. Halterman at Jeri.l.halterman@usace.army.mil and Dave Walsh at david.j.walsh@usace.army.mil with your interest in attending the industry webinar. title: GLWACH Construct Hospital Parking and Renovate Optical Fabrication Laboratory (OFL)
description: W912DQ279A002 REQUEST FOR MARKET INFORMATION / NOTICE OF INDUSTRY WEBINAR FOR GENERAL LEONARD WOOD ARMY COMMUNITY HOSPTIAL (GLWACH) CONSTRUCT HOSPITAL PARKING AND RENOVATE OPTICAL FABRICATION LABORATORY (OFL) PURPOSE: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), Kansas City District, is requesting market intelligence information to identify qualified industry partners capable of supporting a potential Construction Manager at Risk (CMAR) Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a for the stated General Leonard Wood Community Hospital (GLWACH) project at Fort Leonard Wood, MO. The Government is seeking industry feedback to better understand the commercial market interest, market capabilities, market capacity and innovative business practices that may inform the acquisition strategy and structure of the potential OT Agreement. This is not a Request for Qualifications. It does not constitute a commitment by the Government to award an agreement or reimburse respondents for costs associated with responding. Participation is voluntary. PROJECT OVERVIEW and REQUIREMENTS: Project Title: Hospital Parking Lot Construction and Optical Fabrication Laboratory (OFL) Renovation Location: Fort Leonard Wood, Missouri Agency: USACE, Kansas City District (NWK) NAICS Code: 236220-Commerical and Industrial Building Construction Planning and design activities are ongoing. The project�s phased funding profile is listed below: FY23: $31M (Expires September 30, 2027) FY29: $35M (Anticipated) The estimated magnitude for the entire overall effort is between $40 Million and $60M. The new General Leonard Wood Army Community Hospital requires the construction of new hospital parking lots, the renovation of an Optical Fabrication Laboratory (OFL), site work and infrastructure to support the newly constructed GLWACH. The parking lot construction includes site grading and drainage, vehicle circulation roads and parking, pedestrian sidewalks, landscaping (including the planting of trees), site lighting, wayfinding, and video surveillance. The contractor must always maintain 970 parking stalls during construction. The contractor must also ensure safe pedestrian access from the existing parking lots to the new hospital. A construction phasing plan and traffic management plan must be implemented to maintain a safe environment for hospital patrons and staff. The OFL renovation includes the demolition and replacement of the west wall at the current mechanical, electrical, plumbing (MEP) room, removing all equipment inside the MEP and capping all roof penetrations. After demolition the MEP space will remain and become additional storage space for the OFL contract. A new ADA (American with Disabilities Act) compliant entrance vestibule be provided on the west side of the building where the old connection to the hospital was. The OFL also includes the renovation of a medical supply warehouse. To meet life safety codes the optical fabrication lab (OFL) space on the lower level will receive a new egress corridor and lightning protection. The facility must remain fully operational during all deconstruction, demolition, and construction efforts. The former General Leonard Army Community Hospital and infrastructure must be decommissioned, dismantled, demolished, and removed prior to the construction of the new parking lot. This work included the decommissioning of a hospital and clinic, a central utility plant, abatement of hazardous materials and environmental liabilities. All existing paving, utilities, and other site appurtenances, including a helipad, must also be demolished and removed. Approximately 60,000 to 70,000 cubic yards of excavated soil will need to be cut and transported from an adjacent location to the project site for fill. POTENTIAL DELIVERY APPROACH: The Government is evaluating execution of this project using a Construction Manager At Risk (CMAR) Other Transaction Agreement authorized under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a with USACE as the Designer of Record (DOR). Using CMAR OT, the Government is particularly interested in commercial and collaborative practices to determine the following: Phasing and execution strategies to efficiently deliver the project Construction packaging and execution to optimize the given phased funding profile Early and continuous Government-industry collaboration; Collaborative design development and constructability; Contractor-Government open-book cost estimating and cost transparency; Collaborative project phasing and schedule certainty; Collaborative risk identification, mitigation and allocation; Innovation and alternative construction techniques; Overall cost, schedule, and mission outcomes. INDUSTRY INFORMATION REQUESTED: This request is the Government's primary mechanism for obtaining detailed market intelligence regarding industry interest, capability and capacity, relevant experience using CMAR, open-book pricing, and potential commercial practices. The Government welcomes candid industry feedback and recommendations regarding the use the same or similar collaborative commercial practices, agreement terms, project phasing, risk sharing, governance, pricing approaches, and other considerations that could improve successful execution of this project using CMAR under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. Interested firms should complete and submit: The attached Market Intelligence Questionnaire and A summary of their interest and capabilities to perform all the work identified for this project. The summary interest and capabilities is not a formal Request for Qualifications, and the response should not exceed 10 pages in length. The summary should also include the following information: The Company information (name, address, contact information, business structure) Commercial and Government Entity (CAGE) code and/or Unique Entity Identifier (UEI) and SAM.gov registration, if available. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS: Please submit the completed attached questionnaire and a summary of interest and capabilities via email to the individuals listed below no later than: 2:00 p.m. Central Time, 9 October 2026. Jeri L. Halterman at Jeri.l.halterman@usace.army.mil Courtesy copy: Dave Walsh at david.j.walsh@usace.army.mil Interested firms are encouraged to add themselves to the Interested Vendors List associated with this announcement on SAM.gov to receive future updates. INDUSTRY WEBINAR: A virtual Industry Day to better explain the project requirements is scheduled prior to the requested date of submission, Wednesday, September 23, 2026, starting at 2:00 p.m. Central Daylight Time. Please email Jeri L. Halterman at Jeri.l.halterman@usace.army.mil and Dave Walsh at david.j.walsh@usace.army.mil with your interest in attending the industry webinar. Early notification of interest will help us manage the appropriate network band-width necessary for 100% participation. To support this mission, the Government requires a modern software solution that serves as a relational database and analysis toolset. This toolset is essential for the iSMART (interoperable Systems Management and Requirements Transformation) process and is used to populate, edit, analyze, and manage TDL message data, platform implementations, and interoperability evaluations. The Contractor shall provide an existing commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) software solution, including all necessary licenses, updates, training, and technical support. The software shall provide a comprehensive toolset for managing TDL platform specifications, conducting interoperability analysis, and supporting mission planning across the TDL enterprise. The TDL software solution must meet all requirements as listed in the Attachment 1 - Performance Work Statement.
