description: PERFORMANCE WORK STATEMENT (PWS) Department of Veterans Affairs Teleradiology Staffing Services SECTION 1 PURPOSE AND BACKGROUND 1.1 Purpose This Performance Work Statement (PWS) establishes the requirements for teleradiology interpretation services to support STAT and routine priority imaging studies at Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) medical facilities. Based on a 12-month analysis of 17,278 STAT priority imaging studies across five VA facilities (June 2025 May 2026), 41.2% of STAT examinations failed to meet required timeliness standards, representing a significant patient safety and care quality risk. The Government requires a qualified contractor to provide licensed radiologist interpretation staffing services during identified high-risk coverage periods to reduce late reporting rates and ensure Veterans receive timely diagnostic care. 1.1 Background Physician personnel shortages and turnover in the Diagnostic Radiology Services at the covered VA medical facilities have created a significant need for additional professional diagnostic radiology interpretive capacity to ensure that both routine and emergent radiology imaging examinations are always available to Veterans. Contracted teleradiologists will provide final radiology interpretations for exams performed during off tours, and in some cases for exams performed during routine tours when other radiologist services are not available or insufficient to meet clinical demand. The use of teleradiology outsourcing provides a highly cost-effective and expeditious alternative to meet ongoing needs across the covered facilities. Data analysis of STAT imaging volume and timeliness identified three critical coverage gaps: Weekday Overnight Gap (Monday Friday, 8:00 PM 7:30 AM): STAT late rates range from 22% to 60% during overnight hours, with volumes averaging 2 10 studies per overnight shift per facility. Weekend Gap (All Day Saturday and Sunday): Saturday and Sunday represent the highest-volume and worst-performing periods, with late rates reaching 63.6% and average STAT volumes of up to 33 studies per day across facilities. Federal Holiday Gap: Federal holidays represent near-complete coverage failures, with late rates of 75 100% on holidays such as Presidents' Day, MLK Day, Labor Day, and New Year's Day across most covered facilities. The covered facilities use electronic image and health record management and distribution systems including CPRS, VistA Imaging, Philips Intellispace PACS, and Nuance PowerScribe. Contractors with prior experience connecting to VISN 4 radiology systems are preferred. 1.3 Covered Facilities The following VA medical facilities are covered under this contract: Facility Address Altoona VAMC 2907 Pleasant Valley Boulevard, Altoona, PA 16602 Erie VAMC 135 East 38th Street, Erie, PA 16504 Lebanon VAMC 1700 South Lincoln Avenue, Lebanon, PA 17042 Philadelphia VAMC 3900 Woodland Avenue, Philadelphia, PA 19805 Pittsburgh VAMC 4100 Aliquippa Street, Pittsburgh, PA 15240I was in touch with the CO, Erik Whitaker and CS, David Santiago who will be working on this package and is the current CO/CS for Pitt s current contract. They both confirmed that if we added Pitt and Phila into the PWS, they can order off the contract at a later date and it won t be considered out of scope . Wilmington VAMC 1601 Kirkwood Highway, Wilmington, DE 19805 Wilkes-Barre VAMC 1111 East End Boulevard, Wilkes-Barre, PA 18711 * Philadelphia VAMC and Pittsburgh VAMC are not currently placing orders under this contract. However, the awarded vendor must be able to fulfill future orders from these facilities if requested. 1.4 Period of Performance The estimated Period of Performance (POP) for this 5-year contract is from December 31, 2026, to December 30, 2031. SECTION 2 SCOPE OF WORK 2.1 General Scope The Contractor shall provide professional teleradiology staffing services for diagnostic radiology imaging examinations performed at the covered VA medical facilities. Contract services will include off-campus image interpretation via a secure network connection to VA informatics systems, and as needed, providing advice by telephone to clinical providers and radiology technologists regarding protocols or for clarifying questions about radiology exams. The Contractor shall comply with each facility's policies related to reporting of examinations, use of diagnostic codes, and communication of results. The Contractor must be a U.S.-based corporation capable of final interpretation and reporting services via a secure teleradiology network. All services SHALL be performed within the territorial borders of the United States. Contracting to radiologists outside of the territories of the USA is prohibited. The Contractor shall provide all professional personnel and technical support, medical and other equipment, telecommunications, supplies, and supervision necessary to perform, implement, and administer teleradiology services to meet the specific medical needs of the covered facilities. The Contractor is responsible for all Contractor personnel, subcontractors, agents, and anyone acting for or on behalf of the Contractor. 2.2 Modalities Covered The Contractor shall provide interpretation services for the following imaging modalities, which may include imaging of the head, neck, chest, abdomen, pelvis, and extremities: Modality Description Priority Facilities CT / CTA Computed Tomography / CT Angiography All facilities highest volume and highest late rate CR / XR Computed/Digital Radiography (plain film) All facilities high weekend/holiday volume DX Digital Radiography All facilities second-highest volume overall MR / MRA Magnetic Resonance Imaging / MR Angiography Wilkes-Barre, Altoona (limited volumes) US Ultrasound Wilmington, Wilkes-Barre, Altoona, Erie, Pittsburgh (limited volumes) Mammography Diagnostic and screening mammography As occasionally requested, Nuclear Medicine / PET-CT General nuclear medicine and PET/CT As occasionally requested, Diagnostic Radiology / Plain Film (Radiology) Computed Tomography (CT) CT Abdomen & Pelvis (W/O or W & W/O) / CT ABD & Pelvis CT Angiographs / Computed Tomography Angiography CT Angio Abd&Pelv w/o&w/dye / CT SBD & Pelv 1/>REGNS CT Abdomen & Pelvis Multiphase CT Angio Abdominal Arteries w/Runoffs Magnetic Resonance Imaging / Magnetic Resonance (MR) Exam Magnetic Resonance Imaging Angio Magnetic Resonance Imaging Prostate / MR Prostate Ultrasound / Ultrasound (US) Ultrasound - Head and Neck (Thyroid) + Transplants / US Head and neck Ultrasound - OB US Arterial Duplex Nuclear Medicine / Nuclear Medicine (NM) Positron Emission Tomography (PET CT)/Position Emission Tomography (PET)/CT 2D Mammography single breast exam / 2D Mammo 3D Mammography single breast exam / 3D Mammo MRI Cardiac (cpt codes 75557, 75559, 75561, 75563)/Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) Cardiac CT Heart (cpt codes 75572, 75573, 75574) MR Abdomen Exams 2.3 Priority Classification Studies transmitted under this contract shall be classified as either STAT or Routine: STAT: All imaging performed on inpatients and Emergency Department (ED) patients will be considered STAT. Other outpatient studies will be considered STAT if they have been ordered as such or if an expedited interpretation is requested by facility staff. Routine: Outpatient studies not otherwise designated as STAT, with a preferred turnaround of 24 hours and a mandatory turnaround of 48 hours. The Contractor shall not commingle STAT VA studies with routine or non-VA workloads in a manner that degrades turnaround time performance. title: KC135 Life Raft Securing Device
description: The KC-135 fleet currently lacks engineering-approved, standardized methods for securing critical life-saving equipment, presenting a severe risk to crew safety during emergencies. While the raft position aft of the left overwing hatch utilizes secure, hard-mounted straps, the remaining stowage areas�forward of the left overwing hatch and forward of the aft hatch�rely on non-standard, field-expedient restraints such as passenger seatbelts or cargo tie-down straps attached to troop seat support bars. This lack of standardization introduces two critical vulnerabilities: it risks delaying crew evacuation times due to unfamiliarity with varied tie-down methods, and it leaves the crashworthiness of the rafts unverified by engineering authorities. To mitigate these safety risks while minimizing program cost and scope, the position aft of the right hatch will be eliminated from the aircraft configuration. Consequently, this modification effort seeks to develop and implement a field-level Time Compliance Technical Order (TCTO) to standardize and modify the remaining forward-left and forward-aft raft positions, replicating the robust, hard-mounted strap design currently utilized at the aft-left hatch location.

description: he United States ITER Project Office (USIPO) is seeking expressions of interest from qualified suppliers capable of supporting the qualification, commercial-grade dedication, and potential supply of commercially sourced pneumatic components for vacuum systems supporting the ITER project. The anticipated procurement involves pneumatic components used to operate and control vacuum valves and related equipment. The scope is expected to include qualification of selected commercial products to applicable technical and qualification requirements, commercial-grade dedication in accordance with recognized industry guidance, and the development of supporting technical documentation. The anticipated products include approximately 250 pneumatically actuated 3/2-way valve manifolds, 90 air pressure regulators, and 160 pressure relief valves. The procurement may also include an option for the purchase of dedicated hardware from the original equipment manufacturer (OEM), with delivery to Company-designated suppliers and/or the ITER site in France. USIPO is interested in suppliers with demonstrated experience manufacturing and/or supplying pneumatic components for industrial, nuclear, safety-related, or other highly regulated applications. Suppliers should have the capability to support product qualification, commercial-grade dedication, quality documentation, and applicable technical requirements. PROJECT DESCRIPTION: The Department of Veteran Affairs is in the process of migrating from its existing Computerized Patient Record System (CPRS) to the new EHRM platform. The scope of this project includes but is not limited to the following: upgrade facility fiber throughout the buildings to each Telecommunications Room (TR), provide a redundant fiber run throughout the facility to each TR, provide redundant fiber mains to the redundant demarcation rooms from the provider point, install data drops, install new electrical outlets throughout the facility, provide additional power in each TR, upgrade facility power distribution as required, upgrade facility HVAC distribution as required, physical security assessment and upgrades, and hazardous material abatement. In addition to ensuring adequate capacity for planned growth and maintenance, this project addresses deficiencies as defined by the PSRDM (Physical Security Design and Resiliency Manual) 2021 VA Standard. The following buildings have been identified as having deficiencies to address: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 11, 11A, 12, 14, 15, 16A, 21, 22, 24, 27, 34, 35, 35A, 36, 36A, 12A, 14A, 15A, 2B, and site. Project also includes new data center. If additional buildings are found to be integral to patient services, they will be included in the survey and design to ensure that this program is successful and all required connectivity is installed prior to the Go Live date. To date all buildings have been surveyed. PROCUREMENT INFORMATION: The proposed project will be a competitive, firm-fixed-price contract utilizing the Design-Bid-Build approach (Final Specifications and Drawings will be provided). The anticipated solicitation will be issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) in accordance with FAR Part 15, considering Technical Approach, Project Challenges/Phasing & Schedule and Price factors. The results and analysis of the market research will finalize the determination of the procurement method. The type of socio-economic set-aside, if any, will depend upon the responses to this notice and any other information gathered during the market research process. This project is planned for advertising in December 2026. In accordance with Veteran Affairs Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 836.204, the magnitude of construction is between $20,000,000.00 and $50,000,000.00 (Note that the VAAR magnitude of construction is closer to the higher end of this range). The duration of the project is currently estimated at 730 calendar days from the issuance of a Notice to Proceed. The services for this project will include providing all construction related services such as: providing labor, materials and equipment required to complete the project as per contract documents prepared by an independent Architect-Engineer firm. description: Title of Event: Army Data Operations Center (ADOC) Industry Summit � Road to improved data sharing and access in the Army data eco-system Audience: Department of War Contractors and Government Stakeholders When: 27 Oct 2026 Where: Virtual via MS Teams Army Data Operations Center will conduct an Industry Summit on 27 October 2026 via Army MS Teams in order to brief Industry on ADOC activities/capabilities and to inform ADOC Full Operational Capability. Key tasks center around an explanation of what the Army Data Operations Center is, the vision for Army Data Governance and Accessibility, outlining current capability roadmaps, and identifying gaps to Industry and Key DOW Stakeholders. **NOTICE OF SPECIAL INTEREST / INDUSTRY ENGAGEMENT DISCLAIMER** **No Solicitation or Pending RFP:** This announcement is issued solely for information-sharing and market research purposes in support of the Army Data Operations Center (ADOC) Industry Summit. This engagement does not constitute a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), or an Invitation for Bid (IFB). There is no pending contract, solicitation, or procurement action anticipated as a direct result of this event. **No Commitment by the Government:** Participation in the ADOC Industry Summit is completely voluntary. The U.S. Army will not pay for any information submitted, nor will it reimburse vendors for preparation, or any other costs associated with attending or responding to this notice. DOW Briefers include: Army Data Operations Center The Desired End State: ADOC receives and incorporates feedback from Industry Summit participants into the ADOC Lessons Learned Wiki and Rolodex. Industry and DOW Stakeholders have a shared understanding of the Army Data Operations Center�s mission and DOW Data governance & accessibility challenges. This Industry Summit will be held at the CUI level and will be 100% Virtual via Army MS Teams ADOC Focus Areas The Army Data Operations Center (ADOC) is hosting this Industry Summit to foster a technical exchange with industry leaders, innovators, and practitioners. The primary objective is to understand how industry-proven methodologies can be applied to modernize, secure, and scale Army enterprise data infrastructure. During the technical sessions, ADOC is specifically interested in hearing briefings, live demonstrations, and case studies addressing the following core focus areas provided by priority: # Focus Area Participation Criteria 1 Data Platform Support: Describe your current and past performance supporting Army Data platforms (legacy or new systems). What specific technical and operational environments have you actively supported? 2 "As Code" Governance: Detail your methodology and past implementation of "Documentation as Code" and "Policy as Code" within secure DoW or federal enterprise environments to automate governance. 3 Access Control Frameworks: Explain how your solutions implement Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) to enforce security while ensuring secure, mission-appropriate data sharing. 4 Reusability & Products: What is your proven approach to developing stable, discoverable, and reusable baseline data products to reduce duplicate engineering efforts across enterprise platforms? 5 Emerging Trends & AI: How do your solutions leverage AI/ML to optimize governance workflows, analyze request patterns, and improve operational efficiency within a regulated data ecosystem? title: HELICOPTER AERIAL SPRAYING IN NORTH DAKOTA
description: The contractor shall perform chemical application services on federal land administered by the USACE Garrison Project utilizing helicopter-based platforms. Services include 1) proactively surveying said lands for noxious weeds during appropriate growing season(s), 2) inventorying noxious weeds by collecting GPS data (coordinates, weed species, and acres of infestation), 3) controlling noxious weeds via appropriate helicopter chemical application capable of both spot treatment and solid coverage, 4) documenting chemical application services via submittal of completed pesticide application record (PAR)s and collection of global positioning system (GPS) datasets, 5) documenting the degree of noxious weed infestations via preparation and submittal of a comprehensive electronic database, 6) preparation and submittal of invoices for payment of services, and 7) providing proof of application, such as GPS spray tracks, physical or digital maps, etc. will be required. All work shall be completed in accordance with this PWS and all applicable Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) regulations for rotorcraft operations.

description: The Federal Bureau of Prisons is seeking providers for Residential Reentry Center (RRC) beds and Home Confinement services for male and female federal offenders in Berkeley County, West Virginia. Both RRC and Home Confinement services must follow the Federal Bureau of Prisons� Residential Reentry Center, March 2022 Statement of Work. title: USACE Basis of Design J&A for Interior Finishes - Notice of Intent
description: USACE requests a class justification and approval (J&A) for other than full and open competition to allow Contracting Officers to issue solicitations for construction contracts where �brand name or equal� references are necessary to effectively communicate interior color and finish selections. The estimated cost for this class J&A is $230 million, covering projects from Fiscal Year (FY) 27 through FY29. 10 U.S.C � 3204(a)(1) as implemented by the Revolutionary Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Overhaul (RFO) Part 6 and Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS) Class Deviation 2026-O0017, Revision 1. DFARS 206.103-170(c) states �Notwithstanding FAR 6.103-1(d), in accordance with section 888(a) of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2017 (Pub. L. 114-328), the justification and approval addressed in FAR 6.104 is required in order to use brand name or equal descriptions.� This class J&A alleviates the need to execute an individual J&A on a contract-by-contract basis when using such descriptions or specifications in accordance with applicable FAR and DFARS sections. The plans and specifications issued as part of a construction solicitation may include brand name or equal references for architectural finishes that shall be regarded as establishing a standard of quality and shall not be construed as limiting competition to the identified brand. The Contractor may, at its option, use any product that, in the judgement of the Contracting Officer, is equal to that named in the specifications, unless otherwise specifically provided in the contract. This Notice of Intent is not applicable to any single project but covers all construction projects for which the designation of finish colors and/or aesthetic is reasonably anticipated. The funding for these projects encompasses all funds USACE obligates for construction including the Civil Works Mission, the Military Construction Mission and all projects executed by USACE contracting in support of International and Interagency Missions. The individual projects this J&A covers will be solicited across the USACE districts, using whatever acquisition method is deemed most appropriate for the requirement. All responsible sources may submit a capability statement which shall be considered by the agency. title: KC135 Life Raft Securing Device
description: The KC-135 fleet currently lacks engineering-approved, standardized methods for securing critical life-saving equipment, presenting a severe risk to crew safety during emergencies. While the raft position aft of the left overwing hatch utilizes secure, hard-mounted straps, the remaining stowage areas�forward of the left overwing hatch and forward of the aft hatch�rely on non-standard, field-expedient restraints such as passenger seatbelts or cargo tie-down straps attached to troop seat support bars. This lack of standardization introduces two critical vulnerabilities: it risks delaying crew evacuation times due to unfamiliarity with varied tie-down methods, and it leaves the crashworthiness of the rafts unverified by engineering authorities. To mitigate these safety risks while minimizing program cost and scope, the position aft of the right hatch will be eliminated from the aircraft configuration. Consequently, this modification effort seeks to develop and implement a field-level Time Compliance Technical Order (TCTO) to standardize and modify the remaining forward-left and forward-aft raft positions, replicating the robust, hard-mounted strap design currently utilized at the aft-left hatch location.

title: D--Replacement of NWQL's Wastewater Treatment Monitor
description: Replacement of US Geological Survey (USGS), National Water Quality Laboratory's (NWQL) Wastewater Treatment Monitoring Computer System THIS IS A SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE ONLY FOR MARKET RESEARCH PURPOSES. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), REQUEST FOR QUOTATIONS (RFQ) OR INVITATION FOR BID (IFB). NO FORMAL SOLICITATION IS BEING REQUESTED UNDER THIS NOTICE. This Sources Sought Notice is for market research purposes to identify parties having an interest in and resources to support this requirement for replacement of wastewater SCADA computerized control system and software package using Inductive Automation or equivalent software that replicates the functionality of the current SCADA control system with modern, reliable hardware and software while minimizing operational downtime for the US Geological Survey (USGS), National Water Quality Laboratory (NWQL). The result of this market research will contribute to determining the method of procurement. The Government will review the information requested in this announcement based on the responses to this sources sought notice/market research, this requirement may be set-aside for small businesses or procured through full and open competition. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code is 541512 (Computer Systems Design Services) and the size standard is $34.0 million. The following is a brief description of services that are required to be performed: A. Introduction: The US Geological Survey (USGS), National Water Quality Laboratory (NWQL) has a requirement for replacement of wastewater SCADA computerized control system and software package using Inductive Automation or equivalent software Inductive Automation or equivalent software that replicates the functionality of the current SCADA control system with modern, reliable hardware and software while minimizing operational downtime. B. Background: The USGS, NWQL operates a laboratory wastewater and treated ion exchange system. The Safety, Health, and Environmental (SHE) team relies on a computer-based supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) control system to assess discharge performance and maintain environmental compliance. The current system, installed in the mid 2000s, is aging and at risk of failure, which could result in operational shutdown of the laboratory. C. Scope of Work The Contractor shall provide all labor, software, programming, configuration, installation, testing, and documentation required to replace the existing wastewater SCADA control system. D. Technical Requirements: The Contractor shall provide the following: a. Installation, configuration and programming of Ignition Perspective HMI software b. Convert the existing Genesis32 software monitoring screens to Ignition Perspective and integrate logic, alarms and parameter settings. c. Integration of the Ignition Perspective software with the existing Allen Bradley PLC proprietary logic programing owned by others such that integration of the new software does not violate existing intellectual property ownership d. The new Ignition Perspective software will communicate with existing sensors, AB controllers, and treatment system components through the existing proprietary logic developed by others. e. System testing, commissioning, and acceptance verification f. Providing system documentation and operator training E. Functional Requirements: The new system shall: a. Seamless functionality with existing AB PLC proprietary logic programing own by others. b. Replicate and update current monitoring screens and functionality c. Interface with all existing sensors, PLCs, and control hardware d. Accurately measure, display, and record key wastewater parameters e. Provide alarm logic and notifications equivalent to the current system f. Automatically log discharge data for compliance records F. Installation Requirements: The Contractor shall: a. Coordinate installation to minimize downtime b. Ensure all work meets electrical and environmental safety standards c. Perform system cutover in a manner that maintains wastewater compliance capability (End of brief description of Services) If your organization has the potential ability to meet this requirement, please provide the following information to the Contracting Officer: 1. A tailored capability statement describing detailed information in providing wastewater SCADA computerized control system services outlined above. 2. The firm shall specify that they are either: 2.1 A small business, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, etc. and Or 2.2 Other than small business under the NAICS Code listed in the announcement. 2.3 The firm shall provide a point of contact name and e-mail information, and SAM.gov (Unique Entity ID (UEI) and must be registered and active in System for Award Management (SAM). All information submitted in response to this announcement is voluntary � the Government will not pay for information requested nor will it compensate any respondent for any cost incurred in developing information provided to the Government. Materials submitted to the Government for review will not be returned. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation. This is NOT a Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quotations (RFQ) or Invitation for Bid (IFB). The Government does not intend to award a contract based on responses received under this announcement. The government will evaluate market information to ascertain potential market capacity to provide services consistent in scope and scale with those described in this notice and otherwise anticipated. In order to be responsive to this Notice, a firm shall provide the appropriate documentation for consideration by October 9, 2026 at 2:30 p.m. Mountain Daylight Time (MDT). Responses that do not comply with these procedures will not be considered. Telephone inquiries will not be accepted or acknowledged, and no feedback or evaluations will be provided to companies regarding their submissions. Inquiries will only be accepted by e-mail to Lisa Williams at lisa_williams@ios.doi.gov.
